title: The internet
starter: You save a file on a school computer and open it later at home. Describe what has to happen for that to work.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: What is the internet?
facts: A worldwide collection of computer networks: the biggest WAN.
Networks are joined by routers and linked by cables, including undersea fibre.
The World Wide Web is a service that uses the internet; it isn't the internet itself.
stations.challenge: Define the internet in one sentence.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A worldwide collection of computer networks: the biggest WAN.
Also credit: Networks are joined by routers and linked by cables, including undersea fibre.

questions.a: A worldwide collection of connected computer networks

questions.q: What is the World Wide Web?
questions.a: A collection of web pages that are accessed over the internet

stations.name: Domain Name Service (DNS)
facts: People use domain names like www.google.com; computers use IP addresses.
DNS turns a domain name into the matching IP address.
DNS is made up of many domain name servers, not just one.
stations.challenge: Why don't we just type IP addresses into our browsers?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: People use domain names like www.google.com; computers use IP addresses.
Also credit: DNS turns a domain name into the matching IP address.

questions.a: Turns a domain name into an IP address

questions.q: Put the steps in order to show how a browser finds www.google.com.
questions.a: You type www.google.com into the browser → The browser asks a domain name server for the IP address → Domain name servers look up the name, asking other DNS servers if they need to → The IP address is sent back to the browser → The browser requests the page from the web server at that IP address

stations.name: Hosting
facts: Hosting means storing websites, files or services on a server so others can reach them over the internet.
Hosting companies run data centres full of servers and rent out space.
stations.challenge: Why would a small business pay a hosting company instead of running its own web server?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Hosting means storing websites, files or services on a server so others can reach them over the internet.
Also credit: Hosting companies run data centres full of servers and rent out space.

questions.a: Storing websites or files on a server so they can be accessed over the internet

questions.q: Why might a business use a hosting company?
questions.a: It doesn't need to buy, run and look after its own servers

stations.name: The cloud
facts: Storage, software and services on remote servers, accessed over the internet.
Examples: Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive.
You can reach your files from any device, anywhere with a connection.
stations.challenge: What is the advantage of working in the cloud, rather than installing programs and saving files locally?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Storage, software and services on remote servers, accessed over the internet.
Also credit: Examples: Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive.

questions.q: Which is the best description of the cloud?
questions.a: Storage and services on remote servers, reached over the internet

questions.q: Which is a disadvantage of using the cloud?
questions.a: It relies on a stable internet connection

stations.name: Web servers and clients
facts: A web server stores web pages and sends them to clients when they are requested.
A client, such as the browser on your phone, requests a page and displays it.
stations.challenge: Describe the client-server relationship between a web server and a mobile phone.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A web server stores web pages and sends them to clients when they are requested.
Also credit: A client, such as the browser on your phone, requests a page and displays it.

questions.q: In the relationship between a phone and a web server, what is the phone?
What does a web server do?
questions.a: Stores web pages and sends them to clients that request them

stations.name: File servers
facts: A file server stores files centrally for everyone on a network.
A desktop PC is a client: it requests a file, and the file server sends it.
stations.challenge: Describe the relationship between a file server and a desktop PC.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A file server stores files centrally for everyone on a network.
Also credit: A desktop PC is a client: it requests a file, and the file server sends it.

questions.q: Match each device to its role.
questions.a: Web server → Sends web pages to browsers; File server → Stores files for users on a network; Desktop PC opening a file → Client; Phone loading a website → Client

questions.q: Which is an advantage of storing work on a file server?
questions.a: You can open your work from any computer on the network

final.name: Final challenge: the cloud

questions.q: Is each statement an advantage or a disadvantage of the cloud?
questions.a: Copies are kept automatically, so files survive a failed laptop = Advantage; Your files sit on someone else's servers = Disadvantage; A slow connection makes large files painful = Disadvantage; More space can be added the day you need it = Advantage; There's a bill every month for as long as you use it = Disadvantage; No servers to buy, power or replace = Advantage; Nothing works if the internet goes down = Disadvantage; The same files open on any device, anywhere = Advantage

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

points: The World Wide Web is a service that uses the internet; it isn't the internet itself.
Hosting means storing websites, files or services on a server so others can reach them over the internet.
Storage, software and services on remote servers, accessed over the internet.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 2.

A file server stores files centrally for everyone on a network.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
